_note: Single-source (Classic Maya). Mayan sub-palette of the Mesoamerican family; jungle city-states of pyramid-acropolis and stela, the k'uhul ajaw (holy lord) and the Long-Count calendar, bloodletting and the ballgame. civ = feudal. Seeds/shifts Lawful or Neutral. Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Maya register (allowed, catalog 5.3); DEITY names are the Mayan morphs of the Agrippan canon (family_mesoamerican.json theonym_sets.mayan), never real Maya gods.

phonology.palette: Classic/Yucatec Maya: glottalized b'/t'/k'/tz'/ch'; x = sh; vowel length + glottal stop; endings -aj/-il/-an/-tun/-ab; agentive aj- (he of) / ix- (she of); CVC.
phonology.phonotactics: CVC; glottalization; final glottal stop; aspirated stops.

morphology.patronymic_form: the ch'ib'al (lineage) name; aj- (he of) / ix- (she of) prefixes; the k'uhul ajaw line traces its dynasty; calendar-day birth-names.
morphology.compounding_rule: [quality|color](stem) + feature: Chak-witz (red-pyramid), Ek'-nahb (black-lake), Noh-kah (great-town); aj-/ix- + name.

title_ladder.government: feudal (Classic Maya city-states: the k'uhul ajaw (holy lord) over the ajaw nobility and the sajal governors; jungle polities war and ally in shifting hegemonies)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Maya civ, ascending. Built on ajaw (lord): Ajaw (town-king) duchy; K'uhul Ajaw (holy/divine lord) principality; Kalomte' (overlord/high king) kingdom; Noh-Kalomte' (great overlord) empire. Batab' (local chief) barony; Nakom (war-captain) march; Sajal (subordinate governor) county. The ah-k'in priests and the Long-Count calendar order the realm. (Rank titles are the real Maya register, allowed.)

people_name_convention.order: given/calendar-day name + ch'ib'al (lineage); aj-/ix- prefix; the dynastic count for the k'uhul ajaw line; a deed- or war-name.
people_name_convention.dual_register: the ajaw-lineages carry a dynastic name and divine titles; commoners a day-name + lineage.
people_name_convention.theophoric: names invoke the powers (Ixalan's names) + aj-/ix-: e.g. Aj-Tulax, Ix-Rialtaj; calendar-day-and-power names.

religion._note: Deity-names are the Mayan morphs of the Agrippan canon (family_mesoamerican.json theonym_sets.mayan) - never real Maya gods (no Itzamna, Kukulkan, Chaac, Ix Chel, Kinich Ahau). Shared pantheon, Maya names. Ixalan seeds/shifts Lawful or Neutral; its stance follows its CURRENT alignment (see worship_by_alignment). The Long-Count calendar and the bloodletting-rite bind the k'uhul ajaw to the powers; the witz (pyramid) is the altar.
religion.the_one: Aj Ternaj (< Aeternus; the One - revered as the supreme maker and sky-most-high when Lawful, acknowledged but set aside when Neutral)

sample_deity_renames.Maraxus: Marakab (the war-fire, the conqueror; Chaotic power, demonized)

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: revere the One (Aj Ternaj) and the Lawful powers (Tulax, Orlanab, Numench), demonize the Chaotic powers (Marakab, Wakix, Lusankaan)
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: all powers ambivalent - somewhat honored, somewhat feared; foreground the uchben (ancestral dead), the day-lords and local k'uh (spirits)

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the demonized set (the Chaotic powers, when Lawful) take dread epithets: Maraxus -> Marakab the War-Fire; Vacidus -> Wakix the Devourer; Lusanto -> Lusankaan the Hoard-Serpent.
religion.religious_orders_pattern: the K'uh-nah (god-house) atop the witz (pyramid) of [power]: 'the K'uh-nah of Tulax'.
religion.saints_pattern: the deified k'uhul ajaw ancestors (the uchben) and the day-lords, honored at the pyramid-tomb and the carved stela.

holy_symbol_motifs.Numench: a sky-band over the open codex

banks_patterns.ships: riverine and coastal trade-canoes (the great seagoing canoe): 'the Jade Canoe', 'the Quetzal of the Ha''
banks_patterns.military_units: the [k'uhul ajaw] Holkan (warrior-host) / the [animal] companies: 'the Jaguar Holkan', 'the Eagle-warriors'
banks_patterns.taverns: plazas, not taverns - the balche'-house (ritual-mead): 'the Cacao House', 'the Balche' Court'
banks_patterns.dungeons_ruins: vine-choked pyramids and abandoned k'uhul-kah: 'the lost Witz of [ajaw]', 'the Sunken Cenote of [name]'
